titre: Integrating Large Language Models and Metaverse-Related Technologies in Urology Education: Viewpoint.
auteurs: Li P, Gong H, Liu H, Han S, Lu Y, Yan Y.
resume: Unlabelled Urology education must prepare learners to integrate anatomical visualization, diagnostic reasoning, technical performance, communication, and ethical judgment, often under restricted working hours and limited access to high-fidelity cases. This viewpoint argues that large language models (LLMs) and metaverse-related technologies should be integrated as complementary, supervised educational tools rather than treated as autonomous replacements for educators or clinical experience. LLMs can support cognitive apprenticeship, documentation practice, assessment, and communication simulations, whereas extended reality, cloud computing, and virtual digital humans can support spatial, procedural, and remote learning. Our aim is to articulate 3 key messages: first, the educational value of these technologies depends on alignment with defined urological competencies; second, implementation should proceed in stages from governed data infrastructure to intelligent interaction and immersive multimodal training; and third, educational effectiveness must be established through prospective evaluations of transfer to clinical performance, not through technical novelty alone. We emphasize the need for rigorous randomized controlled trials, identify requirements for haptic and biomechanical fidelity, and discuss hallucination, bias, privacy, accountability, and deskilling. The responsible future of intelligent urology education will therefore require collaboration among learners, educators, clinicians, engineers, ethicists, institutions, and professional bodies.

titre: Neutrophil to Lymphocyte Ratio and Neurological Outcome in Ischemic Stroke at 4.5 to 24 Hours: A Post Hoc Analysis of TRACE-III Trial.
auteurs: Hao M, Ma Y, Wang L, Jin A, Law ZK, Campbell BCV, Schwamm LH, Parsons MW, Fisher M, Xu Y, Xu A, Cao Z, Wang L, Wu S, Wang Y, Xiong Y.
resume: Introduction Whether neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR), as a marker of increased inflammatory response, modifies the efficacy and safety of tenecteplase is uncertain in patients 4.5-24 h after stroke onset. We investigated this in the Tenecteplase Reperfusion Therapy in Acute Ischemic Cerebrovascular Events-III (TRACE-III) trial. Methods TRACE-III was a phase 3, multicenter, prospective, open-label, randomized, blinded-endpoint trial that enrolled 516 patients from 58 centers in China between January 2022 and November 2023. Patients had anterior large vessel occlusion and evidence of salvageable brain tissue on perfusion imaging, presented 4.5-24 h after symptom onset, and were randomized 1:1 to intravenous tenecteplase (intervention) or standard medical treatment (control). The primary efficacy and safety outcomes were modified Rankin scale score of 0-1 at 90 days and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or death, respectively. This post hoc analysis in 513 patients with complete admission NLR data compared outcomes in patients with elevated NLR (> first quartile) and non-elevated NLR (≤ first quartile). Results In the elevated NLR group (> 3.0), tenecteplase was associated with increased functional independence (61 [30.2%] vs. 36 [19.6%]; adjusted relative rate [aRR] 1.51; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05-2.17; P = 0.03) compared to standard medical treatment. This benefit was not observed in the non-elevated NLR group (26 [41.9%] vs. 25 [38.5%]; aRR 1.12; 95% CI 0.73-1.73). Safety outcomes did not differ in either the elevated or non-elevated NLR groups. Conclusion Baseline NLR may provide a potential signal for differential treatment response to intravenous tenecteplase in patients with acute ischemic stroke, although these exploratory findings require further validation in independent studies. Trial registration TRACE-III is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05141305.

titre: Video Decision Support and Advance Care Planning in Older Adults With Advanced Kidney Disease: The VIDEO-KD Randomized Clinical Trial.
auteurs: Volandes AE, Lakin JR, Chang Y, Lindvall C, Quintiliani LM, Lundquist AL, Liu A, Tamura MK, Unruh M, Wong SPY, Davis AD, Garde C, Henault L, Samarakoon U, Hanchate A, Mandel E, Green JA, Lawson K, Ran
resume: Older adults with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) face consequential decisions about whether to initiate dialysis, yet advance care planning (ACP), the communication that prepares patients for such decisions, is documented infrequently in ambulatory settings. To determine whether a video decision aid about treatment options for advanced CKD, combined with patient-created video declarations, increases ACP documentation among older adults with advanced CKD. This multicenter, parallel-group randomized clinical trial was conducted at 12 ambulatory clinics from June 2021 to March 2025, with 12-month follow-up. Participants were adults 65 years or older with advanced CKD. Outcome assessors were masked to group assignment. Data were analyzed in April 2026. Intervention participants viewed a certified video decision aid depicting 3 treatment options for advanced CKD (hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, and conservative kidney management) and then created a video declaration, a recorded statement of goals, values, and treatment preferences in video, audio, or written format, that was sent to their treating clinician. Control participants received usual medical care. The primary outcome was ACP documentation in the electronic health record within 12 months of enrollment or death, whichever came sooner. Documentation was ascertained by validated natural language processing-assisted human adjudication. Prespecified secondary outcomes included documented discussion of kidney failure treatment options and stated treatment preferences. A total of 453 patients were included (228 intervention [50.3%] and 225 control [49.7%]; mean [SD] age, 78.8 [6.4] years; 190 women [41.9%]; 4 American Indian or Alaska Native [1.1%], 8 Asian [1.8%], 38 Black [8.4%], 35 Hispanic or Latino [7.7%], 3 Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander [0.7%], and 375 White [82.8%] individuals). At 12 months, ACP documentation was higher in the intervention group than the control group (56.6% vs 40.0%; rate difference, 16.6%; 95% CI, 7.5%-25.7%; P < .001), as was documented discussion of kidney failure treatment options (46.1% vs 31.6%; rate difference, 14.5%; 95% CI, 5.6%-23.4%; P = .001). After viewing the video, fewer intervention participants than controls at enrollment were undecided about treatment (30 of 227 [13.2%] vs 92 of 223 [41.3%]), and more preferred conservative kidney management (115 of 227 [50.7%] vs 71 of 223 [31.8%]; P < .001 for the overall distribution). This randomized clinical trial found that, among older adults with advanced CKD, a video decision aid increased ACP documentation and reduced the proportion of patients who were undecided about treatment. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04347629.

titre: Real-world renoprotective effects of polyethylene glycol-loxenatide in type 2 diabetes: a multicenter, ambispective cohort study.
auteurs: Ye J, Li J, Chen Y, Chen F, Zhu D, Zhang C, Chen Q, Tian Y, Yang S, Xu W, Xie B, Chen ZS, Hou K.
resume: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease face persistent risks despite standard care. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide lacks real-world renoprotective evidence in high-risk Chinese populations relative to non-incretin-based standard care. This multicenter, ambispective cohort study enrolled 3305 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, renal impairment, and elevated cardiovascular risk at six Chinese tertiary institutions (median follow-up 36.4 months; trial registration: ChiCTR2300073001). Data were extracted via an artificial intelligence-enhanced pipeline. Co-primary analyzes comprised multivariable-adjusted Cox regression and 1:1 propensity score matching (332 per group); pre-specified landmark analyzes at 6 and 12 months addressed immortal time bias. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide was associated with a reduced risk of the primary kidney composite outcome in the original cohort (hazard ratio [HR], 0.49; 95% CI, 0.25-0.95; P = 0.035), which was corroborated in the propensity score matched cohort (HR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.20-0.97; P = 0.043) and progressive across 6-month (HR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.19-0.84) and 12-month (HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.14-0.75) landmarks. While a reduction in 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events was observed in the unmatched cohort (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43-0.85; P = 0.004), this association was not sustained in the matched analysis (HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.57-1.48; P = 0.735). In conclusion, long-term therapy was associated with an attenuated risk of major renal events. Given the null findings in the matched cohort, the cardiovascular observations are exploratory and require randomized confirmation.

titre: Beyond Taxonomy: Fungal Nutraceutical Supplementation Modifies the Functional Potential of the Gut Microbiome in Colorectal Cancer.
auteurs: Rodríguez-Costas N, Rodríguez-Blanco A, Expósito CR, Cubiella J, Stompel ES, Fernández-de-Ana Portela C, Martín AID, Taboada-Rodríguez P, Silva BF, Fernández MDR, Zarraquiños S, Remedios D, Gómez CAS,
types: brief-report randomized controlled trial journal article
resume: The gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of host immune regulation, intestinal homeostasis, and recovery after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Although our previous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial demonstrated that fungal nutraceutical supplementation with Micodigest ® was associated with favorable taxonomic and systemic inflammatory changes in patients undergoing CRC surgery with curative intent, the functional consequences of this intervention remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a functional metagenomic analysis of fecal samples collected from patients enrolled in the original clinical trial to investigate whether Micodigest ® supplementation was associated with changes in the functional potential of the gut microbiome. A total of 37 patients were analyzed, including 24 receiving Micodigest ® and 13 receiving placebo, with paired samples collected before supplementation and after 4-6 weeks of intervention. Shallow shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed, and microbial functional potential was characterized using KEGG Orthologues (KOs). Differential abundance analysis identified 14 significantly different KOs between groups at baseline and 23 after intervention, with no overlap between the two sets of orthologues. Following supplementation, Micodigest ® -treated patients exhibited increased representation of functions related to CRISPR-associated systems, bacteriophage biology, and chitin-derived carbohydrate utilization, together with reduced representation of nutrient acquisition systems, conjugative transfer, sulfur metabolism, and components of the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway. These functional signatures suggest coordinated changes in microbial ecological adaptation, nutrient utilization, genetic exchange, and metabolic activity following fungal nutraceutical supplementation. Integration with previously reported taxonomic and inflammatory findings supports the hypothesis that Micodigest ® may promote coordinated remodeling of the gut microbiome and host-microbiota interactions during the perioperative period. Although the present study cannot establish causality or directly infer microbial activity from metagenomic potential, these findings provide novel functional insights into the microbiome response to fungal nutraceutical supplementation in patients with CRC and highlight functional metagenomics as a valuable complement to taxonomic profiling.

titre: Expanded Longitudinal Validation of Adaptive Learning Stability in AI-Assisted Neurosurgical Residency Training.
auteurs: Mustafayev B, Mustafayeva A, Bakhtiyarov A, Nikatov K, Satylkhan B, Mustafayev A.
types: validation study randomized controlled trial journal article
resume: Objective To evaluate the longitudinal stability, reproducibility, and robustness of Adaptive Learning Stability (ALS) within an expanded AI-assisted neurosurgical residency cohort during a 12-month observation cycle. Design This was a prospective controlled educational study. Residents completed 4 consecutive quarterly checkpoints integrating cognitive, technical, and decision-making assessments over 12 months. The RCKaS-AI framework incorporated predictive analytics, individualized adaptive remediation, and mentor-validated feedback pathways. Primary analysis evaluated longitudinal entrustment trajectory stability across checkpoints. Secondary analyses included inter-resident variance dynamics, remediation frequency, faculty workload, and predictive agreement between forecasted and observed competency progression. Setting Two accredited neurosurgical residency programs in Kazakhstan, from January 2025 to January 2026. Participants Sixty-four neurosurgical residents randomized into standard RCKaS (n = 32) and AI-enhanced RCKaS-AI (n = 32) cohorts. Results Both cohorts demonstrated progressive improvement in entrustment scores across sequential checkpoints. In the RCKaS-AI cohort, mean entrustment scores increased from 59.1 ± 12.8 at CP1 to 94.3 ± 6.9 at CP4, compared with 58.4 ± 13.1 to 85.7 ± 10.4 under standard RCKaS conditions (p = 0.001). Inter-resident variance decreased by 41% in the AI-assisted cohort versus 18% in the standard cohort. Residents within the RCKaS-AI framework achieved entrustment level 4 significantly earlier than controls (38 ± 7 weeks vs 50 ± 9 weeks, p = 0.003). Mean remediation frequency decreased from 3.4 ± 1.1 to 1.9 ± 0.7 sessions per resident, while faculty workload declined by 34%. Predictive analytics demonstrated strong agreement between forecasted and observed competency trajectories (r = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.77-0.89). Conclusions Expanded longitudinal implementation of the RCKaS-AI framework demonstrated reproducible stabilization of competency trajectories during neurosurgical residency training. These findings support the robustness of adaptive AI-assisted feedback systems as a practical mechanism for longitudinal competency regulation within structured surgical education programs. Further multicenter validation is required to evaluate external reproducibility across broader residency environments.
